metadata.case_name: MO PO v. YAT FAI ENGINEERING LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: fixing wooden formwork / nailing wooden battens

injuries.description: penetrating injury to the left eye-ball
source: (i) The Plaintiff has suffered a penetrating injury to the left eye-ball which required three operations under general anaesthetic with the prospect of a further operation to extract a cataract and implant an intra-ocular lens. His best corrected visual acuity to his left eye is 6/12 [a 50% loss of central vision]. He has a traumatic cataract of the left eye. The left pupil is abnormal. It is slightly oval and slightly dilated with reaction to light being sluggish.
injuries.icd_description: Penetrating wound of eyeball without foreign body, unilateral

injuries.description: traumatic cataract of the left eye
source: He has a traumatic cataract of the left eye.

(i) The Plaintiff has suffered a penetrating injury to the left eye-ball which required three operations under general anaesthetic with the prospect of a further operation to extract a cataract and implant an intra-ocular lens.

manifestations.description: Best corrected visual acuity to his left eye is 6/12 (a 50% loss of central vision)
Photophobia (undue sensitivity to sunlight) with pain and excessive tearing (as alleged by Plaintiff and Dr Ng)
Reduced working capacity — judge assessed working capacity as 15 days per month (reduced ability to work a full month)

treatments_future: extraction of cataract and implantation of an intra-ocular lens

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenity for penetrating injury to the left eyeball (including visual loss, photophobia, abnormal pupil)

Loss of earning capacity and reduced ability to work (monthly pre-accident earnings assessed at $18,000; reduced working capacity assessed at $12,000/month; award for loss of earning capacity noted as $144,000)

comparable_cases.case_name: Sze Ping Chui v Lau Ching Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: Plaintiff had sustained a ruptured eye-ball and underwent an operation to repair the cornea, to remove the damaged lens and to implant an intra-ocular lens. He was left with blurred vision, a corneal scar and photophobia. Visual acuity was 35% of normal.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Kin Ka v Siu Tung Hun
comparable_cases.injury_description: Best corrected acuity was 44% of normal and plaintiff could not resume his pre-accident work.

comparable_cases.case_name: Kei Yu Fuk v Wong Ching Nam
comparable_cases.injury_description: Penetrating injury caused by a metal fragment resulting in central eye vision of 20/80; difficulty in perception of depth and in judging distances.
